docs.title: create-go-starter
docs.text: A powerful CLI tool to generate production-ready Go projects in seconds.

docs.title: info About
docs.text:
create-go-starter is a stable, production-ready CLI generator for modern Go applications.

  • check Stable version - v1.4.0 available
  • check 3 templates - minimal, full, GraphQL
  • check Tested and validated - Used in production
  • check Open source - MIT License
  • check Actively maintained - Regular updates

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: create-go-starter is a Go project generator that creates a complete hexagonal architecture with all the essential features of a modern backend application. With a single command, get a structured project with JWT authentication, REST API, database, tests, and Docker configuration ready for deployment.

docs.title: Included Features
docs.text:
• Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) - Clear separation of concerns
  • JWT Authentication - Access tokens + Refresh tokens with secure rotation
  • REST API with Fiber v2 - High-performance web framework
  • Database - GORM with PostgreSQL and automatic migrations
  • Dependency Injection - uber-go/fx for modular architecture
  • Complete Tests - Unit and integration tests included
  • Swagger Documentation - Automatically documented API with OpenAPI
  • Docker - Optimized multi-stage build and docker-compose
  • CI/CD - Pre-configured GitHub Actions pipeline
  • Structured Logging - rs/zerolog for professional logs
  • Validation - go-playground/validator for input validation
  • Makefile - Useful commands for dev, test, build and deployment

docs.title: new_releases New in v1.2.0: CRUD Generator
docs.text:
Add new models in 2 seconds! The add-model command automatically generates all the necessary CRUD code:

cd my-project
create-go-starter add-model Todo --fields "title:string,completed:bool"

What is automatically generated: - check Model with GORM tags - check Repository (interface + implementation) - check Service (business logic) - check HTTP Handlers (REST endpoints) - check Tests (unit + integration) - check Routes, migrations, fx modules

Supported relations: - --belongs-to Parent - N:1 relation (child → parent) - --has-many Child - 1:N relation (parent → children)

Example with relations: 

create-go-starter add-model Category --fields "name:string:unique"
create-go-starter add-model Post --fields "title:string,content:string" --belongs-to Category
create-go-starter add-model Comment --fields "author:string,content:string" --belongs-to Post

Result: Complete blog (Category → Post → Comment) with nested endpoints and preloading.

arrow_forward Full add-model guide

docs.title: new_releases New in v1.3.0: Advanced Observability
docs.text:
Production-ready monitoring in one command! The --observability=advanced flag generates a complete observability stack:

create-go-starter my-app --template=full --observability=advanced

What is automatically generated: - check Prometheus Metrics — /metrics endpoint with HTTP metrics (latency, throughput, errors) - check Distributed Tracing — OpenTelemetry + Jaeger with W3C traceparent propagation - check K8s Health Checks — /health/liveness and /health/readiness with DB verification - check Grafana Dashboard — Pre-configured 7-panel dashboard with alerting - check Docker Compose — Complete stack (Jaeger + Prometheus + Grafana) - check Kubernetes Probes — Auto-generated probes.yaml file

arrow_forward Full observability guide

docs.title: Method 1: Direct Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
Global installation with a single command, without cloning the repository:

go install github.com/tky0065/go-starter-kit/cmd/create-go-starter@latest

The binary will be installed in $GOPATH/bin (usually ~/go/bin). Make sure this directory is in your PATH.

Note: If create-go-starter is not recognized after installation, add $GOPATH/bin to your PATH:

export PATH=$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin

docs.title: Method 2: Build from Sources
docs.text:
Recommended for contributors or customization:

git clone https://github.com/tky0065/go-starter-kit.git
cd go-starter-kit
go build -o create-go-starter ./cmd/create-go-starter

docs.title: Get Started in 30 Seconds
docs.text:
# 1. Install the tool
go install github.com/tky0065/go-starter-kit/cmd/create-go-starter@latest

# 2. Check your environment
create-go-starter doctor

# 3. Create a project
create-go-starter my-project

# 4. Automatic setup
cd my-project
./setup.sh

# 5. Run
make run

# 6. Test
curl http://localhost:8080/health

docs.title: CLI Architecture
docs.text: Technical documentation for contributors explaining how create-go-starter works internally.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The CLI is built with zero external dependencies - it uses only the Go standard library.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
cmd/create-go-starter/
├── main.go              # CLI entry point, custom flag parsing, color utilities
├── generator.go         # File generation orchestrator (build + write), validation
├── templates.go         # Core infrastructure templates (server, db, config)
├── templates_user.go    # User domain templates (handlers, services, auth)
├── interactive.go       # Interactive mode (--interactive / -i)
├── dryrun.go            # Dry-run preview (--dry-run / -n)
├── doctor.go            # Doctor command (environment diagnostics)
├── progress.go          # Progress bar for file generation
├── stats.go             # Generation statistics display
├── version.go           # Version constant
└── *_test.go            # Tests co-located with source files

docs.title: main.go
docs.text:
• CLI entry point
  • Custom flag parsing (replaced stdlib flag package for alias support)
  • Short aliases: -t, -d, -o, -i, -n, -h
  • Color utilities for terminal output
  • Sub-command dispatch (doctor, add-model)
  • Main function orchestration

docs.title: generator.go
docs.text:
• Project directory creation
  • Two-phase generation: build*FileList() then writeFiles()
  • Project name validation
  • Error handling
  • Dry-run support (build without write)

docs.title: interactive.go
docs.text:
• Step-by-step guided wizard using bufio.NewReader
  • Project name input with validation
  • Template, database, observability selection
  • Configuration summary with confirmation
  • Zero external dependencies

docs.title: dryrun.go
docs.text:
• Displays files that would be generated without creating them
  • Shows configuration summary
  • File and directory count
  • Existing directory warnings

docs.title: doctor.go
docs.text:
• Environment diagnostics command
  • Go version check (>= 1.21)
  • Git availability check
  • Docker binary + daemon status check
  • Colored pass/fail output

docs.title: progress.go / stats.go
docs.text:
• Visual progress bar during file generation
  • Auto-disables on non-TTY or NO_COLOR environments
  • Generation statistics (files created, directories, duration)

docs.title: templates.go / templates_user.go
docs.text:
• Template definitions using string concatenation
  • Project name interpolation
  • All generated file contents

docs.title: Template Pattern
docs.text:
Templates use string concatenation (not text/template):

func (t *ProjectTemplates) GoModTemplate() string {
    return `module ` + t.projectName + `

go 1.25.5
`
}

docs.title: Adding New Templates
docs.text:
1. Add template method to ProjectTemplates
  2. Add file entry in the build*FileList() function in generator.go
  3. Add tests for the new template

docs.title: Hexagonal Architecture
docs.text:
Generated projects follow the hexagonal architecture (Ports & Adapters) pattern:

graph LR
    subgraph "Primary Adapters"
        HTTP[HTTP Handlers]
    end

    subgraph "Application Core"
        SVC[Domain Services]
        PORT[Ports/Interfaces]
    end

    subgraph "Secondary Adapters"
        REPO[Repositories]
        DB[(Database)]
    end

    HTTP --> PORT
    PORT --> SVC
    SVC --> PORT
    PORT --> REPO
    REPO --> DB

docs.title: 1. Create Domain Entity
docs.text:
// internal/models/product.go
type Product struct {
    ID    uint   `gorm:"primaryKey"`
    Name  string `gorm:"not null"`
    Price float64
}

docs.title: 2. Define Interface (Port)
docs.text:
// internal/interfaces/product_repository.go
type ProductRepository interface {
    Create(ctx context.Context, product *models.Product) error
    FindByID(ctx context.Context, id uint) (*models.Product, error)
}

docs.title: 3. Implement Repository (Adapter)
docs.text:
// internal/adapters/repository/product_repository.go
type productRepository struct {
    db *gorm.DB
}

func (r *productRepository) Create(ctx context.Context, product *models.Product) error {
    return r.db.WithContext(ctx).Create(product).Error
}

docs.title: 4. Create Service (Domain)
docs.text:
// internal/domain/product/service.go
type Service struct {
    repo interfaces.ProductRepository
}

func (s *Service) CreateProduct(ctx context.Context, name string, price float64) (*models.Product, error) {
    product := &models.Product{Name: name, Price: price}
    return product, s.repo.Create(ctx, product)
}

docs.text:
// internal/adapters/handlers/product_handler.go
func (h *ProductHandler) Create(c *fiber.Ctx) error {
    // Parse request, call service, return response
}

docs.text:
• Go 1.25 or higher - Check your version with go version

go version
# Should display: go version go1.25.x ...

If Go is not installed, download it from golang.org/dl.

docs.title: Method 1: Direct Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
Global installation with a single command, without cloning the repository.

go install github.com/tky0065/go-starter-kit/cmd/create-go-starter@latest

This command:

  • Automatically downloads the code from GitHub
  • Compiles the binary
  • Installs it in $GOPATH/bin (usually ~/go/bin)
  • Makes it globally available

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
create-go-starter --help

You can also run the doctor command to verify your environment is correctly set up:

create-go-starter doctor

Note: Make sure $GOPATH/bin is in your PATH:

export PATH=$PATH:$(go env GOPATH)/bin

docs.title: Tutorial: Complete Example
docs.text: A step-by-step tutorial to create and develop a complete project.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will:

  1. Create a new project
  2. Configure the environment
  3. Test the API
  4. Add a new feature
  5. Deploy with Docker

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Project
docs.text:
# Install the tool
go install github.com/tky0065/go-starter-kit/cmd/create-go-starter@latest

# Create project
create-go-starter blog-api
cd blog-api

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Environment
docs.text:
# Automatic setup
./setup.sh

# Or manual setup
go mod tidy
echo "JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32)" >> .env

# Start PostgreSQL
docker run -d --name postgres \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=blog-api \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  postgres:16-alpine

docs.title: Step 3: Run and Test
docs.text:
# Start the application
make run

# In another terminal, test the API
curl http://localhost:8080/health
# {"status":"ok"}

# Register a user
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/register \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@blog.com","password":"admin123"}'

# Login
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@blog.com","password":"admin123"}'

// internal/models/post.go
package models

import "time"

type Post struct {
    ID        uint      `gorm:"primaryKey" json:"id"`
    Title     string    `gorm:"not null" json:"title"`
    Content   string    `gorm:"type:text" json:"content"`
    AuthorID  uint      `json:"author_id"`
    Author    User      `gorm:"foreignKey:AuthorID" json:"author,omitempty"`
    CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
    UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
}

docs.title: 4.2 Add Migration
docs.text:
Update internal/infrastructure/database/database.go:

db.AutoMigrate(&models.User{}, &models.RefreshToken{}, &models.Post{})

docs.title: 4.3 Create Interface
docs.text:
// internal/interfaces/post_repository.go
package interfaces

type PostRepository interface {
    Create(ctx context.Context, post *models.Post) error
    FindByID(ctx context.Context, id uint) (*models.Post, error)
    FindAll(ctx context.Context) ([]models.Post, error)
    Update(ctx context.Context, post *models.Post) error
    Delete(ctx context.Context, id uint) error
}

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide details the usage of create-go-starter and explains the structure of generated projects.

docs.title: Basic Command
docs.text:
The basic syntax is very simple:

create-go-starter <project-name>

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
create-go-starter my-api-backend

This command will create a new my-api-backend/ directory with the entire project structure using the full template by default.

docs.title: Flags and Aliases
docs.text:
All flags have short aliases for faster typing.

Flag Alias Default Description --help -h Show help --interactive -i false Launch guided interactive mode --dry-run -n false Preview files without creating them --template -t full Template: minimal, full, graphql --database -d postgres Database: postgres, mysql, sqlite --observability -o none Observability: none, basic, advanced

Sub-commands:

Command Description doctor Environment diagnostics (Go, Git, Docker) add-model Generate a CRUD model in an existing project

Flexible syntax: Flags accept = or space as separator: 

# These syntaxes are equivalent:
create-go-starter -t=minimal my-app
create-go-starter -t minimal my-app
create-go-starter --template=minimal my-app
create-go-starter --template minimal my-app

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Minimal template
create-go-starter my-project --template minimal
create-go-starter my-project -t minimal

# Full template (default)
create-go-starter my-project --template full
create-go-starter my-project  # Same result

# GraphQL template
create-go-starter my-project --template graphql
create-go-starter my-project -t graphql

# Choose MySQL as database
create-go-starter my-project --database=mysql
create-go-starter my-project -d mysql

# Choose SQLite (ideal for prototyping)
create-go-starter my-project --database=sqlite
create-go-starter my-project -d sqlite

# Combine template and database
create-go-starter my-project --template=minimal --database=sqlite
create-go-starter my-project -t minimal -d sqlite

# Dry-run: preview without creating files
create-go-starter my-project --dry-run
create-go-starter my-project -n

# Dry-run with specific options
create-go-starter my-project -t minimal -d sqlite -n

# Guided interactive mode
create-go-starter --interactive
create-go-starter -i

# Full combination with observability
create-go-starter my-project -t full -d postgres -o advanced

Notes: - The --template flag is optional. If not specified, the full template is used by default. - The --database flag is optional. If not specified, PostgreSQL is used by default. - The --dry-run flag is optional. It displays the list of files that would be generated without creating them. - The --interactive flag launches a guided assistant and ignores other configuration flags.

docs.title: Interactive Mode (--interactive) new_releases
docs.text: New in v1.4.0! Interactive mode guides the user step by step to configure a new project.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
create-go-starter --interactive
create-go-starter -i

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Interactive mode asks for:

  1. Project name -- With real-time validation
  2. Template -- Choice between minimal, full (default), graphql
  3. Database -- Choice between postgres (default), mysql, sqlite
  4. Observability -- Choice between none (default), basic, advanced (if full template)
  5. Summary -- Display of chosen configuration with confirmation
create-go-starter - Interactive Mode

Enter project name: my-app
Select template (minimal/full/graphql) [full]: full
Select database (postgres/mysql/sqlite) [postgres]: postgres
Select observability (none/basic/advanced) [none]: advanced

Configuration Summary:
  Project:       my-app
  Template:      full
  Database:      postgres
  Observability: advanced

Proceed with generation? (y/n) [y]: y

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• info Interactive mode requires an interactive terminal (no stdin pipe)
  • warning --interactive and --dry-run cannot be used together
  • info Zero external dependencies -- uses only bufio.NewReader from stdlib

docs.title: Dry-Run Preview (--dry-run) new_releases
docs.text: New in v1.4.0! Dry-run mode displays the files that would be generated without creating them.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
create-go-starter my-app --dry-run
create-go-starter -n -t minimal -d sqlite my-app

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Dry-run displays: - The configuration used (template, database, observability) - The complete list of files that would be created - The number of files and directories - A warning if the target directory already exists

Dry-run mode: no files will be created

  ...

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text: The project name must follow certain rules:

docs.title: Allowed Characters
docs.text:
• Letters: a-z, A-Z
  • Numbers: 0-9
  • Hyphens: -
  • Underscores: _

docs.title: Restrictions
docs.text:
• No spaces
  • No special characters (/, \, @, #, etc.)
  • No dots (.)
  • Must start with a letter or number

docs.title: Valid Examples
docs.text:
create-go-starter my-project           # OK
create-go-starter my-awesome-api       # OK
create-go-starter user_service         # OK

docs.title: Invalid Examples
docs.text:
create-go-starter my project           # Space not allowed
create-go-starter my-project!          # Special character
create-go-starter -my-project          # Starts with hyphen

docs.title: Generated Structure
docs.text:
Here's the complete structure created by create-go-starter:

my-project/
├── cmd/
│   └── main.go                    # Application entry point
├── internal/
│   ├── models/                    # Shared domain entities
│   ├── domain/                    # Business logic layer
│   │   └── user/
│   │       ├── service.go
│   │       └── module.go
│   ├── adapters/                  # HTTP handlers, repositories
│   │   ├── handlers/
│   │   ├── middleware/
│   │   └── repository/
│   ├── infrastructure/            # DB, server configuration
│   │   ├── database/
│   │   └── server/
│   └── interfaces/                # Ports (interfaces)
├── pkg/                           # Reusable packages
│   ├── auth/
│   ├── config/
│   └── logger/
├── .github/workflows/ci.yml
├── .env
├── Dockerfile
├── Makefile
└── go.mod

docs.title: Option A: Automatic Setup (Recommended)
docs.text:
cd my-project
./setup.sh
make run

docs.title: Option B: Manual Setup
docs.text:
cd my-project

# Generate JWT secret
openssl rand -base64 32
# Add to .env: JWT_SECRET=<generated_secret>

# Install dependencies
go mod tidy

# Start PostgreSQL
docker run -d --name postgres \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=my-project \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  postgres:16-alpine

# Run the application
make run
